title: PhonePe Wins UAE Central Bank Licence for First-Ever Foreign Foray
excerpt: Founder Sameer Nigam says the fintech will launch a local wallet, gift cards, diaspora remittances and merchant acquiring in the Emirates — and aims to be "a global business" within a decade.
body:
• PhonePe has received a licence from the Central Bank of the UAE and will soon launch local operations there — its first market outside India.
  • Founder Sameer Nigam announced the move on the sidelines of the Global Fintech Festival, saying the company will be "a global business" within a decade.
  • The licence covers a local wallet, gift cards, diaspora remittance services and merchant acquiring in the Emirates.
  • The IPO-bound fintech leads India's UPI market; Nigam declined to comment on domestic UPI merchant fees ahead of the share sale.

PhonePe, India's largest digital payments company, is going global. The fintech announced on Wednesday that it has received a licence from the Central Bank of the UAE and will soon begin operations in the Emirates — its first foray outside India.

Founder and chief executive Sameer Nigam disclosed the development to reporters on the sidelines of the annual Global Fintech Festival in Mumbai. "PhonePe will be launching its local operations in the UAE as our first foreign market," he said, adding that over the next ten years the company expects to be a global business.

What the licence allows

The central bank licence is a broad one. It permits PhonePe to launch its own wallet in the UAE, issue gift cards, offer remittance services aimed at the diaspora, and handle local merchant acquiring — effectively replicating much of its Indian playbook in a new market.

https://x.com/gaze_observer/status/2097929981955616960

"If you are a UAE citizen, hopefully in the near future you will be able to make payments on a UAE point of sale device and also send money to India," Nigam said, sketching a vision in which the company's rails carry everyday transactions at both ends of the India-UAE corridor.

Why the UAE comes first

The choice of market is no accident. The Emirates hosts one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities, and the India-UAE remittance corridor is among the busiest on the planet. A wallet that lets workers in Dubai pay locally and send money home through a familiar Indian app plugs directly into that flow.

PhonePe already dominates at home, holding the highest market share among UPI payments apps. Taking that scale abroad is a natural next step for a company that has spent a decade building distribution — more than 71.5 crore registered users and a merchant network topping 5 crore, as of July 2026.

The IPO question

The expansion announcement lands as PhonePe prepares for a public listing. Nigam declined to comment on the introduction of a merchant discount rate (MDR) for UPI transactions in India — a live policy debate with direct bearing on fintech revenues — quipping only that he would be able to speak about the share sale once clarity emerges on the MDR question.

Investors will be watching whether the UAE experiment can become a template. Cross-border payments and diaspora remittances are high-margin businesses compared with domestic UPI, where transaction economics remain razor-thin. A successful UAE launch would give PhonePe a growth story beyond India's borders to take to the public markets.

What to watch

The immediate milestone is operationalisation of the licence — hiring, local partnerships and the first live transactions. Competition will be stiff: the Gulf's payments market already hosts deep-pocketed regional players and global card networks. But PhonePe arrives with something few rivals have — a brand already trusted by hundreds of millions of Indians, many of whose families live and work in the Emirates.
